clue.text: Hard worker one of those responsible for horse and trap

definitions.meaning: to work like a ... is to toil tirelessly, so a tireless toiler is one

definitions.text: one of those responsible for horse and trap
definitions.meaning: the Greeks hid in a wooden horse at Troy; the citizens of Troy hauled it in, springing the trap on themselves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and trap' poses as a pony and cart; the horse is the one left at Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the name for a citizen of ancient Troy, famed for toil and for the wooden horse.

clue.text: Soak last of fruit in port to make this dish

indicators.note: in places the drunkard and the letter inside the port's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, short form Rio
a soak is a drunkard, as is a sot

indicators.note: last of tells us to take only the final letter of the word fruit

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: steep the end of the fruit in port wine to make this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' looks like a verb and 'port' like the wine; one is a drunkard (noun), the other a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock is a classic plated meal.

clue.text: He views the action from a box

definitions.text: He views the action from a box

parts.words: He views the action from a box
parts.note: reads like a theatregoer in a box seat, but the action is a lawsuit and the box is where twelve people sit in court

explanation.definitionFit: A member of a court's jury sits in the jury box and watches a legal action unfold.

clue.text: Beginning to develop sickbay erected with little cash

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the word is built upwards, so sickbay's letters read from the bottom

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a school sickbay
a cent is a small coin, a little cash

explanation.surface: A clinic being built with very little money is only just getting started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns SAN upwards into NAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is emerging, just coming into existence.

clue.text: Militant is in Berlin following fourth part of play

indicators.note: following says the German word comes after the stage division in the answer

parts.note: an act is a main division of a play
IV is the Roman numeral for four
ist is German for is, the word used in Berlin

explanation.surface: A radical is in Berlin after the fourth act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: IV is the Roman numeral for four, giving ACT IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A militant campaigner for a cause is a vigorous campaigner, a synonym.

clue.text: Material point grasped by Nym, for one

indicators.note: grasped by says the compass point is held inside the soldier's rank

parts.note: Nym is a corporal in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A tip taken in hand by a man named Nym becomes stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporal Nym is a Shakespearean rogue, one of Falstaff's cronies; 'for one' marks him as an example of the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily, physical, tangible: material in that sense.

clue.text: Inactivity could be nice, pocketing new benefit

indicators.note: pocketing means the rearranged letters put the other pieces in their pocket, around them
could be suggests the letters of nice may become something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: the fodder as written
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Doing nothing might be pleasant, while collecting fresh welfare money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' shuffles NICE into I...NCE, which holds N and DOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is laziness, a habit of idleness.

clue.text: Beginning event with Greek character replacing daughter

indicators.note: replacing says the Greek letter takes the place of the daughter's letter

parts.note: an incident is an event or happening
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A happening opens with a figure from Greece standing in for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' is an adjective here: just starting, as in an early stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipient means in an initial stage, starting to emerge.

clue.text: It establishes ownership of river in noble's possession

indicators.note: in with possession says the river is held inside the noble's word
in someone's possession means held by them, so the river sits inside

parts.note: noble means aristocratic, titled; the 's governs the possession
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A deed proving property rights to a river held by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in someone's possession' means held by them, so the river is held within the aristocratic word.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document proving who holds property is the deed of ownership.

clue.text: Celebrity backing way to become national leader

indicators.note: backing says the way's two letters within the celebrity's word turn round

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A famous person retreats along a road to rule the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing way' reverses only the ST at the front of STAR, giving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the emperor and ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Racy cadets ragged timid fellow

indicators.note: ragged means teased or roughed up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the fodder as written

explanation.surface: Lively trainee officers tease a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' is the anagram indicator, British slang for teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaredy-cat is a childish word for a coward, someone easily frightened.

clue.text: It prevents one, sinking in a difficult situation

definitions.meaning: in old golf, a ball blocking the line between an opponent's ball and the hole stopped that putt going down
a predicament or impasse where you are blocked

explanation.walkthrough: 'sinking' is a golfer's word: holing a putt. The comma makes 'one, sinking' read like a drowning.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf term for an obstructing ball broadened to mean any obstacle or tight spot.

clue.text: Cave in wood sheltering everyone on way back

indicators.note: sheltering means the wood surrounds and protects the other piece

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: on way back means the word for everyone travels in reverse

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A cave in a wood where everyone takes cover on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' poses as a noun; with 'in' it is the verb phrase to fall inwards. 'on way back' turns ALL to LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall in on itself, which is to cave in.

clue.text: County coach, provides position for foremost players

parts.note: Down is a county in Northern Ireland
a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: A coach from a county gives the lead actors their spot.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNTY DOWN is in Northern Ireland; 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstage is the front of a stage nearest the audience, where leading actors stand.

clue.text: He may have a warrant to lead strikers on the march

definitions.text: He may have a warrant to lead strikers on the march

parts.words: He may have a warrant to lead strikers on the march
parts.note: reads as a police officer arresting picketing workers; the warrant is an army rank and the strikers beat drums in a band

explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a military marching band is often a warrant officer, heading the drummers.

clue.text: Saving system set up by House, in readiness for a rainy day

definitions.text: Saving system set up by House, in readiness for a rainy day

parts.words: Saving system set up by House, in readiness for a rainy day
parts.note: reads as a parliamentary savings scheme for hard times; really a barrel beside a house collecting rainwater

explanation.definitionFit: A barrel set at a house's downpipe stores rainwater for later use in the garden.

clue.text: Traits one developed as a shopkeeper

indicators.note: developed means the letters grow into a new form, rearranged

parts.note: the fodder as written

explanation.surface: Characteristics a person built up while running a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges TRAITS ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a retailer selling paper, pens and office supplies.

clue.text: Original model made by roguish Eastern characters

parts.note: arch means mischievous or roguish
type means printed characters, letters

explanation.surface: A prototype built by mischievous folk from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' poses as people; it is printers' type.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is a prototype or perfect example from which copies follow.

clue.text: French resort accommodating English relative

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the resort holds the English letter

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A Riviera town putting up an English kinswoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Section of cult rather extreme in opinion

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a sect holds rather radical views.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person holding extreme views, especially in politics.

clue.text: Gathered together and composed

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is assembled in one place; the other is calm, poised and in control.

clue.text: State of a solid figure, expressed briefly

parts.note: LA is the abbreviation for Louisiana, a US state
conic means cone-shaped, a solid geometrical figure

explanation.surface: A geometry problem about the condition of a solid shape, put in few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as condition; it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means terse, using very few words.

clue.text: Delicacy — one a king consumed by a grotto

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten up by, so the pieces go inside the grotto's word

parts.note: a grotto is a cave
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A treat; a monarch eaten up in a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: An old spelling of fish roe; the first 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare, salted sturgeon roe, is a luxury food.

clue.text: Show lively interest, taking in directions in this way

indicators.note: taking in means the directions hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: ENE, east-north-east, is a compass direction combining several
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: Getting excited while following instructions like this.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to express eager excitement.

clue.text: Disciplinarian can initially spoil film

indicators.note: initially says the word for spoil comes first, ahead of the can

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a tin is a can
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A strict superior may first wreck a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' poses as a verb; it is a container. 'initially' says the spoiling word leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict enforcer of rules.

clue.text: A rodent keeps it in a hole

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the rodent goes round the word it

parts.note: a cavy is a guinea pig, a rodent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature has something hidden in its burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow space or hole.

clue.text: Hired worker, one bit by bit accepted by 3

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the clue-3 word
bit by bit means the word one enters in separate portions

parts.note: 3 refers to the answer to clue 3, the member of a jury
the word one, split into O and NE
the word one, split into O and NE

explanation.surface: A hired hand gradually admitted by a juror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit by bit' splits the word one into two portions, each slotted separately into the clue-3 word.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified craftsman working for wages under someone else.

clue.text: Meet a stated target

indicators.note: stated means spoken aloud, so the word for target is heard as a conjunction

parts.note: a butt is a target, as at archery

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit a declared aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' poses as a verb of greeting; it means to adjoin.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to touch along a border, to adjoin.

clue.text: Answered snappily, looking embarrassed about rich cake

indicators.note: about means around, so the colour surrounds the cake

parts.note: red is the colour of a blushing, embarrassed face
a torte is a rich cake

explanation.surface: Someone blushing over a gateau gave a sharp reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Retorted means made a quick sharp reply.

clue.text: Spiteful-sounding yarn

indicators.note: sounding says the word for spiteful is heard, giving a homophone

parts.note: spiteful means cruel

explanation.surface: A nasty-sounding tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' tempts as a story; it is embroidery wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool used for embroidery.
